title: AI-Supported Workload Reduction for Nurses Through a New Care Model for Geriatric Patients with a History of Falls
summary: Many people over the age of 80 experience at least one fall per year, which significantly impacts their independence. The fear of further falls often leads to reduced mobility and an increased need for care. At the same time, nurses are under significant strain due to a shortage of skilled workers. The SAVE&SAFE project is developing a new model of care (NVF) to address these challenges. A key component of the NVF is the introduction of a specially trained nurses, the "Fall Prevention Specialist" (SVP), who is responsible for preventing falls and coordinating care after hospital discharge. The SVP takes on tasks such as assessing fall risks and implementing preventive measures, thereby reducing the workload of nurses (primary effect) and preventing subsequent falls (patients) (secondary effect). Additionally, an Intelligent Care System (iPS) is installed in patient rooms to detect and automatically document mobility-related events. The project examines how this innovative model of care impacts the workload of nurses and the fall incidence among patients. The intervention is being implemented in three geriatric hospitals: in Krefeld (Alexianer GmbH), Düsseldorf (Alexianer GmbH), and Bonn (Johanniter Hospital).
conditions: Fall prevention in acute geriatrics, AI-based assistance system for monitoring mobility and fall events in geriatric patients

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients must be at least 70 years old at the time of inclusion. They must have an increased fall risk, as determined by clinical assessment, along with geriatric typical multimorbidity (at least three diseases) and polypharmacy (at least five active ingredients) after a fall event within the last 12 months. They must be able to walk at least 4 meters with or without aids, and their Mini-Mental Status Examination (MMSE) must be at least 18 points. Additionally, patients should have sufficient knowledge of the German language.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with terminal-stage diseases or severe advanced dementia (MMSE < 18) are excluded from the study.
